notes: Two bullets, both on the same NPC, so one marker that never moves. The only real decision is the OR: the header and bullet 2 both offer 3x Silk Thread OR 3x Crawler Calculus, and that is exactly what items_alt is for, so it is modelled rather than flattened to one of the two. The page writes the plural 'Crawler Calculus' in the item requirement and 'Crawler Calculus' again in bullet 2; the singular is what resolves (id 1156) -- 'Crawler Calculi' does not resolve at all, so the singular is used. Both sub-bullets under bullet 2 are sourcing advice (who sells thread, what drops the calculi) and are not steps. The reward is 600 gil, so nothing in this quest is observable and every evidence field is null.

notes: A two-rung limit-break quest on one NPC. The second half of the Item Reqs -- four unspent merit points -- is a real gate that no packet this addon reads reports, so it is recorded only as a note and the quest is demoted to medium for it; the crest count alone will show ready when the player may not be. 'Nomad Moogle' is in the resolver's AMBIGUOUS_NPCS set (there is one in every city), so the step zone Ru'Lude Gardens is what makes the marker safe -- it must not be dropped. The nested sub-bullets under bullet 2 are ways to acquire seals (Login Campaign points, Shemo's 3:1 exchange) and are not steps; note also that they talk about seals while the quest wants crests, which is the wiki being loose rather than a second requirement. The reward is a level cap raise, so there is nothing observable to hang evidence on anywhere.

notes:
Bullet 1 is not really part of this quest -- it is the header's Quest Reqs restated: you must already have bought the 'Sakura and the Holy Grail' key item after roughly a hundred rearing interactions. It is kept as an optional precondition rung rather than dropped, because it is the only thing on the page that tells a player why the quest will not start. Its key item does NOT resolve under any spelling I tried (ki, item, upper and lower case), so it cannot be evidence and the rung carries none; that unmodellable gate is why the quest is medium.

The page also does not say where Zenicca stands. The surrounding sentence is all Mog Garden and the Skipper Moogle certainly is one, but guessing a zone costs the step its marker if the guess is wrong, whereas leaving it null costs nothing here -- 'zenicca' is not an ambiguous name, so a nil zone still resolves. Zenicca and a Skipper Moogle are alternatives, and an OR of two TARGETS has no expression in this schema (items_alt is items, not targets), so only the named one is the target and the moogle is a note.

The header's giver is the Green Thumb Moogle and the walkthrough never speaks to it -- bullet 2 opens the quest with a cutscene on entering the Mog Garden. The header string is kept as the start because it resolves and the Green Thumb Moogle is a real standing entity in that zone, but the flag records that what actually fires is a zone entry. Bullet 4's 'Rearing Grounds' is a sub-area of the Mog Garden, not a zone of its own, so the step keeps zone Mog Garden and the location goes in the note.

The Auction House route has no place and no target, so it cannot be a rung at all; the Bubbly Bernie route does, and it splits into two -- a trade of the Quus to the ??? by the South Gustaberg lighthouse, which pops him, and the kill, which drops the clock. Neither is marked optional, because the Steam Clock sitting on step 3 as evidence already handles the other route correctly: a player who bought one on the AH satisfies step 3 the instant they hold it and the mark jumps straight to Malene, which is exactly right.

The ??? is in OBJECT_DENY and can never carry a marker, but it keeps its rung -- the grid (M-10) is the only location information the page gives and losing the rung would lose it. Bullet 3 ends with 'you must zone out of Bastok Markets once' and bullet 4 is the return, so those really are two rungs on Michea with an unmarkable zone-out between them; the page does put it there, so it stays. Two consecutive rungs on one NPC draw as one marker anyway.

notes:
Six numbered bullets that are only three actions. Bullet 2 ('she will return the Moon pendant to you') is the OUTCOME of bullet 1, not a step, so it becomes step 1's evidence -- the pendant is granted there, which is where rule 3 says it belongs. Bullet 3 is walking directions and merges into the note of the ??? rung.

Bullets 4 and 5 are the same ??? examined twice with nothing between them, so they are one rung, exactly like the Blank Target in Divine Might. The tempting evidence for bullet 5 is the Emerald abyssite of expertise -- and it must NOT be used, because it is the header's Reward field verbatim: it proves the quest is over, not that a rung is done. That is the one real trap on this page and the flag records it.

The Moon pendant is buried at the ???, so it leaves inventory partway through and the ladder falls back on the session latch for the return trip; there is nothing observable left after the burial. Fame 'aalt' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only the raw string is kept. 'Alisa (A)' is the wiki's Abyssea suffix form and the normaliser folds it to 'alisa', so it is written as the page writes it. notes:
The whole quest is bullet 3, and it is the Lure of the Wildcat shape: nine Waypoints in one zone, no order given or implied, and a strict ladder would mark one of them and go quiet until the player happened to walk into it. So all nine share a group and draw at once, each with its own grid.

The parenthesised strings in the list -- 'Platea Triumphus (COU Co.)', 'Pioneers' Coalition', 'Auction house', 'Your Rent-a-Room' -- are BUILDINGS, not entity names; the thing you attune to is the Waypoint, which resolves cleanly and is not in the resolver's ambiguous set. Each building name goes in that rung's note where it belongs. There is no observable progress at all here: attunement is a per-character flag, not an item, so every evidence field is null and nothing can track how many of the nine are done.

Bullet 2 is not a step but a shortcut -- if you already attuned everything before taking the quest, you just talk to Alienor again -- so it is folded into the final turn-in's source bullets and note. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine fame regions and does not resolve, so it gates nothing; the raw string is kept.

notes:
The header files 'Ancient tablet fragment' under Item Reqs, but it is a KEY item (ki id 274) and does not resolve as an item at all -- getting that wrong would have cost the middle of the ladder its evidence, which is the whole point of probing before writing.

The five ???s in the Quicksand Caves are ONE rung, not five. Only one is live at a time and it respawns at a random one of the five the moment it is found, so there is no order to record and no way to know which grid to point at; the rung therefore carries no grid and the five locations, with their map numbers, go in the note. That is the As Thick as Thieves six-tower shape. The rung is unmarkable anyway -- '???' is in OBJECT_DENY -- but it keeps its place and its zone.

Bullet 3 hands over TWO key items at once and both are granted there, so both are its evidence as a single AND-list; neither appears anywhere else in the quest, so the duplicate gate is clean. Bullet 4 says 'speak to' Charlaimagnat, not trade, so no items are claimed on that rung even though you are carrying both key items to him. Bullet 5's zone-and-wait-one-earth-minute is real time, which nothing observable reports, and the payoff is the Teleport-Altep scroll -- a reward, so not evidence. Fame 'r' is the wiki's Rabao abbreviation and resolves to the rabao_selbina region.
